# kind: # Scenes (friday, tickets, turn, outro) are designed pages in video/scenes and carry their own text, so they have no subtitle.

name: friday
spoken: Friday, four p.m. A partner goes live Monday, and their web app needs access to every API. It is one line of configuration. In twenty-four APIs, owned by six teams.

name: tickets
spoken: So one line becomes twenty-four tickets, reviews and deploys. Some get stuck. Monday comes, and the launch is not ready. It lands on Thursday.

name: turn
spoken: The rule is the same in every API. So why is it stored twenty-four times? Tyk five sixteen adds API Fragments.

name: blocked
line1: NovaPay's web app calls all 24 Meridian APIs through Tyk Gateway
line2: The browser blocks every one: NovaPay is not an allowed origin
spoken: This is the partner's web app, calling all twenty-four APIs through Tyk Gateway. The browser blocks every one.

name: manager
line1: Fragments have their own screen in Tyk Dashboard
line2: Each one is a named piece of shared API configuration
spoken: Fragments have their own screen in the Dashboard, under Assets.

name: usage
line1: The Fragment lists every API that uses it
line2: 24 APIs reference this one CORS policy
spoken: Each Fragment lists the APIs that reference it. Twenty-four APIs share this CORS policy.

name: edit
line1: Add the partner's origin to the Fragment
spoken: The platform team adds the partner's origin once, and saves.

name: allowed
line2: All 24 APIs now accept NovaPay. No API was edited or redeployed
spoken: Reload the partner app. All twenty-four APIs accept it. No API was edited or redeployed.

name: badge
line1: API teams see what is shared, and which Fragment sets it
line2: The setting is read-only inside the API
spoken: In each API, the shared setting is marked and read-only, with the Fragment that sets it.

name: guard
line1: Now a mistake: a value of the wrong type
line2: Tyk checks all 24 APIs first and refuses the save
spoken: Now a mistake: a value of the wrong type. Tyk checks every API that uses the Fragment and refuses the save.

name: still
spoken: Nothing was saved, and the partner app still works.

name: outro
spoken: Twenty-four APIs, one edit, no tickets. Store shared configuration once, and Tyk refuses a change that would break the APIs that use it.
